theme: Bless the LORD, O my soul
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 103. It is one of the most beloved psalms of praise. David speaks to his own soul, and recounts the benefits of God: forgiveness, healing, redemption, and compassion. Read it slowly.
settingTheScene: Psalm 103 is a psalm of David. It opens with a self-address: “Bless the LORD, O my soul.” Then it moves through a list of God’s benefits, his character, his compassion for human weakness, and his everlasting throne. It ends with a call to the angels and all creation to bless him. Reading it after John 13 to 14 makes us see the love of the Father which Jesus came to show.
observation: “Bless the LORD, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless his holy name!” (v. 1).
“Who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases” (v. 3).
“The LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love” (v. 8).
“He does not deal with us according to our sins, nor repay us according to our iniquities” (v. 10).
“As far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our transgressions from us” (v. 12).
“As a father shows compassion to his children, so the LORD shows compassion to those who fear him” (v. 13).
“For he knows our frame; he remembers that we are dust” (v. 14).
“But the steadfast love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him” (v. 17).
interpretation:
David talks to himself. “Bless the LORD, O my soul, and all that is within me.” He gathers up his whole being, mind, heart, and will, to praise. And he reminds himself not to forget God’s benefits. We tend to forget. The list begins with the greatest: God forgives all our iniquity. He heals all our diseases. He redeems our life from the pit. He crowns us with steadfast love and mercy. He satisfies us with good, so that our youth is renewed like the eagle’s.

Verse 8 is a quotation of what God said to Moses on Sinai: “merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.” It is the heart of the Old Testament’s picture of God. He does not always accuse or keep his anger forever. “He does not deal with us according to our sins.” If he did, none of us would survive. Instead, as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his steadfast love toward those who fear him. “As far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our transgressions from us.” East and west never meet. Our sins are gone.

Then comes the tender image of a father: “As a father shows compassion to his children, so the LORD shows compassion to those who fear him.” Jesus came to reveal the Father in this way. “For he knows our frame; he remembers that we are dust.” God is not surprised by our weakness. He knows what we are made of. Human life is brief, like grass, but the steadfast love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting.

The psalm ends with a widening circle of praise. God’s throne is established in the heavens, and his kingdom rules over all. Angels, mighty ones, hosts, and all his works in all places are called to bless the LORD. And the psalm ends where it began: “Bless the LORD, O my soul!”

How can God forgive sin so completely and still be just? The cross answers that question. The Father removed our transgressions as far as the east is from the west because the Son bore them.
connection: Exodus 34:6-7 is the source of verse 8. Isaiah 40:6-8 contrasts the grass with the word of God. Micah 7:18-19 says God casts all our sins into the depths of the sea. Isaiah 38:17 says he has cast all my sins behind his back. Luke 15:20 is the father running to the prodigal. Romans 3:25-26 explains how God is just and the justifier. Ephesians 1:7 says in him we have redemption through his blood. Hebrews 8:12 promises that he will remember our sins no more.
application:
Write a list of God’s benefits to you, as David did. Read it aloud and give thanks.

Take a sin you cannot forgive in yourself and place it as far as the east is from the west.

Speak to your own soul: “Bless the LORD, O my soul.”
prayerPrompts: Bless the LORD with all that is within you.
Name a benefit of his that you do not want to forget.
Thank him that he removes your sin as far as the east is from the west.
